SpaceX Bull 2X ETF⬇️

World’s largest provider of leveraged and inverse ETFs set to debut single-stock ETF on same day as SpaceX’s IPO.

BETHESDA, Md.—ProShares, the world’s leader in geared (leveraged and inverse) investing, today announced plans to launch ProShares Ultra SpaceX (SPCF) targeting 2x daily returns of SpaceX on the same day that SpaceX is scheduled to go public, June 12, 2026.

SpaceX has become a foundational player in global connectivity, AI, and the space economy. The company is aiming to raise $75 billion in its initial public offering, which would make it the largest IPO valuation in history at $1.75 trillion.1

“SPCF intends to offer investors a way to magnify a bullish view on SpaceX without borrowing on margin on the day of SpaceX’s IPO,” said ProShares CEO Michael L. Sapir. “Investors will be able to target 2x daily returns of SpaceX with the convenience and transparency of an ETF.”

ProShares offers the world’s largest lineup of geared ETFs, with more than 115 funds and over $90 billion in assets across equities, fixed income, commodities, currencies, crypto, and volatility.2 SPCF joins ProShares’ lineup of single-stock ETFs, including funds targeting 2x daily returns of Circle, Coinbase, NVIDIA, Palantir and Tesla.

title: Strategy For Using Leveraged ETFs Instead Of Options Contracts To Make More Money
snippet:
Strategy For Using Leveraged ETFs Instead Of Options Contracts To Make More Money

The reason you buy options is because you want leverage to make more money.
 
ETFs and options can express the exact same directional view, but there are scenarios where a leveraged ETF is the better choice and vice versa.

Take $TSLA as an example.

If I’m bullish, I can buy calls. Or I can use something like $TSLT, $TSLL or $TSLR for roughly +2x leverage daily exposure.

If I’m bearish, $TSLQ targets roughly −2x the daily move.

Let's breakdown Leveraged ETFs vs Options

1. A leveraged ETF resets every day.

This is probably the most important thing to understand.

A 2x ETF seeks 2x of today’s move. It doesn't promise 2x the return of the underlying over a week, month or year. There's slippage from one day to another!

If the underlying gains 10% today and another 10% tomorrow, it’s up maybe 21%.

A perfectly tracking 2x vehicle would gain 20%, reset, then gain another 20% on its new NAV: +44%. Trending markets can actually make daily compounding work in your favor.

But the opposite is true.

A +10% move followed by −9% puts the underlying almost exactly back where it started. You slip.

The 2x vehicle goes +20%, then −18.18% from its new NAV.

Result: roughly −1.8% despite the stock being flat.

title: Such interesting times in my favorite commodities: #uranium, #silver, #copper, and #fluorspar.
snippet:
Such interesting times in my favorite commodities: #uranium, #silver, #copper, and #fluorspar.
Plenty of volatility, but nothing that changes the powerful fundamentals. The supercycle has just started and will continue for many years. A few words about each commodity followed by my top picks:

                                     Uranium
Structural supply deficit meets accelerating nuclear build-out. With new reactors, life extensions, and SMRs advancing globally, utilities remain under-contracted and prices must move much higher to incentivize new mine supply.

                                        Silver
A rare combination of monetary metal and critical industrial input. Exploding solar demand and limited primary mine supply are tightening the market, while any renewed investment flows could amplify upside. Physical supply drained, vaults soon empty?

                                      Copper
The backbone of electrification. Grid expansion, EVs, and urbanization are driving demand growth just as permitting delays and declining ore grades constrain supply, a classic setup for sustained higher prices.

                                   Fluorspar
Quietly indispensable. Essential for steel, aluminum, uranium conversion, and lithium-ion batteries, yet produced in only a few countries. Western supply security efforts could re-rate this overlooked critical mineral.

title: Crypto Daily – August 23, 2026
snippet:
Crypto Daily – August 23, 2026
Institutional inflows collide with governance exploits and regulatory fragmentation.

Market Overview
Bitcoin’s 22% rally to $77,160 this week was driven by record U.S. spot ETF inflows—$1.92 billion into Bitcoin funds and $697 million into Ethereum products —but the surge also triggered $547 million in liquidations, leaving 90,000 traders exposed. Ethereum outperformed with a 30% gain, while altcoins like XRP and Hyperliquid saw sharper moves, reflecting a rotation into higher-risk assets. The rally’s fragility became clear when $100 billion was wiped from total market cap in an hour, underscoring the role of leverage over organic demand. Beneath the volatility, structural shifts are underway: LayerZero’s decision to sunset support for 14 blockchains by September mirrors broader consolidation in interoperability infrastructure, while Nigeria’s SEC and Pakistan’s PVARA are tightening oversight of offshore exchanges.

Bessent also said “no one is above the reach” of U.S. sanctions, including China-linked entities, as President Trump pushes world leaders to further isolate Iran economically.

title: Daily Market Report #662
snippet:
Daily Market Report #662

It’s Tuesday, and March began with a geopolitical landscape that has completely shifted.

We are now seeing another war unfolding in the Middle East, with the United States and Israel against Iran. Iran has responded by targeting neighboring regions, which has created uncertainty across the Gulf. In Dubai, housing prices have started to fall. There was already a bubble forming, and now uncertainty is accelerating the correction.

The Strait of Hormuz is partially closed, affecting global oil flows. LNG facilities in Qatar, which supply Europe, have reportedly been hit. Gas prices are rising. Gold jumped to $5,300, while silver is sitting at $86, slightly down from its recent highs. The broader market initially reacted negatively to the news. There is talk that this conflict could last only weeks, but the real question is the aftermath.

At the same time, the war in Ukraine continues, and tensions around Taiwan remain. The question many are asking is what is stopping China from making a move on Taiwan. That would be a true black swan event. On top of that, last week’s PPI and core inflation numbers came in higher than expected, complicating the macro outlook after what had been a relatively stable start to 2025.
